hints: Notice the words immediately distilled, as this tells you whether oxidation of the alcohol stops early or goes all the way.
Propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, so gentle distillation gives you propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$.
Think about what happens when an aldehyde undergoes nucleophilic addition with HCN, and how the C=O bond changes.
walkthrough:
**Decide the oxidation product**

Remember, primary alcohols give aldehydes when distilled, but carboxylic acids when heated under reflux.

Here the mixture is immediately distilled, so oxidation stops at the aldehyde:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[O], distil} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify the type of reaction with HCN**

Aldehydes and ketones react with HCN in the presence of KCN by nucleophilic addition to form cyanohydrins.

The general change is:
$$\text{RCHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{RCH(OH)CN}$$

**Apply to propanal**

Put the ethyl group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$ in place of R.

You get 2-hydroxybutanenitrile:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Conclude the product**

This is a hydroxynitrile with 4 carbons, one OH and one CN on the same carbon. That matches the cyanohydrin of propanal.

options.A: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{C(CN)(OH)CH}_3$, the cyanohydrin of propanone. You would only get this if you started from propan-2-ol (a secondary alcohol) oxidised to a ketone, then added HCN. Our starting alcohol is propan-1-ol, so this is incorrect.
options.B: This formula $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is butanoic acid with 4 carbons. Even full oxidation of propan-1-ol under reflux would only give propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, with 3 carbons. It also ignores the HCN addition step completely.
options.C: Correct and well done. Distillation gives propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, and nucleophilic addition of HCN gives its cyanohydrin, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$. Both the carbon skeleton and the functional groups fit perfectly.
options.D: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, a straight nitrile with no OH group. HCN with carbonyls gives addition to form a hydroxynitrile, not substitution of OH by CN. This product would come from a halogenoalkane with KCN, not from an aldehyde with HCN.
